assumptions.choice: Both EMAs computed on the Close price series
assumptions.reason: Spec states EMA periods but not which price to apply them to; Close is the standard convention for crossover systems.
Spec gives '10,000 units' only as an example ('e.g.'); exposed as a parameter with that example as the default so it can be overridden.

assumptions.choice: Implemented as two separate orders on a reversing crossover: self.close() to flatten the existing position, followed by self.buy()/self.sell(size=UNITS) to open the new fixed-size position, both submitted in the same bar
assumptions.reason: Spec lists 'close' and 'open' as two distinct rules rather than a single doubled-size reversal order; both orders fill at the next bar's price so the resulting position and total commission are identical to a single combined order, while trade logging cleanly separates the closed trade's P/L from the newly opened trade.

assumptions.choice: A list (self.orders) tracks all outstanding orders (up to two on a reversal bar) and next() takes no new action while any are pending, clearing entries on Completed/Canceled/Margin/Rejected
assumptions.reason: Canonical default #5 requires guarding pending orders; extended to a list because a reversal bar can submit two orders instead of one.

assumptions.choice: Implemented via print() calls inside notify_order (timestamp, price, side) and notify_trade (timestamp, pnl/pnlcomm on close), not at module level
assumptions.reason: Spec requires trades be logged with timestamps, prices, and P/L on close; print() inside strategy methods is instance-level runtime behavior, not top-level executing code, so it does not violate the no-prints-at-module-level constraint.

assumptions.choice: Used the harness-provided single 1-minute AAPL data feed as-is; no resampling
assumptions.reason: Spec's 'M1 or D' timeframe language is illustrative and the execution environment fixes the feed to 1-minute bars with no other data available.
